newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says he seeks no confrontation with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he seeks no confrontation with Iraq.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Monday the United States sought no confrontation with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein but declined to say whether that meant he would forego immediate air strikes on Iraq.

"We have sought no confrontation with Saddam Hussein," Clinton said when asked by a reporter whether Iraq's agreement to stop challenging allied planes patrolling no-fly zones meant the United States "can forego any immedicate further airstrikes."

Clinton said he wanted to answer carefully in light of tensions raised by the continuing possibility of strikes against Iraqi targets by U.S. forces in the Gulf, but he avoided any conclusive statement on whether the likelihood of that were now diminishing.
"My concern is that we limit Saddam Hussein's ability to threaten his neighbors, that we do it with the no-fly zones and that we keep our pilots safe," he said.
Clinton sent U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry on a swift tour of Gulf allied states over the weekend in a bid to shore up support for any U.S. strike against Iraq.

The United States began building up forces in the region for such a strike last week after Iraq repeatedly challenged allied planes patrolling no-fly zones in northern and southern Iraq. But allied support for such retaliation was tepid at best and further declined after Saddam's government annouunced it was stopping its challenges.
